title: Tool Schema Definition Language (TDSL) and Runtime Validation Playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: The current runtime accepts a loosely defined JSON schema for tool/function parameters. This leads to inconsistent validation errors across SDKs, poor developer UX when a call fails, and brittle backward compatibility when schemas evolve. Goal: Define a compact, expressive tool schema definition language (TDSL) that can be authored by model/tool owners and consumed by the runtime and SDKs. Provide clear server-side validation semantics, deterministic error classes, and an interop compatibility layer for legacy schemas. Deliver a playbook for authors, runtime behavior, and rollout steps.
acceptance_criteria:
- TDSL spec v1 document (human + machine readable) published in docs.
- Runtime implements TDSL parser and validation with deterministic error codes for all validation failures.
- SDKs (python/js/go) use server error codes to map to friendly messages and local preflight checks.
- Backward compatibility shim translates legacy schemas into TDSL with warnings.
- End-to-end tests covering schema evolution (add optional, rename with alias, deprecate param) and examples validated in CI.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
1) Language: TDSL is a small JSON/YAML-first shape DSL with annotations for: type, required/optional, coercion rules, constraints (min/max/regex), canonical name, alias list, deprecation info, and 'compatibility' hints (allow_unknown_keys: bool).
2) Validation semantics: server performs strict validation by default. Modes: strict | permissive | legacy-shim. Strict -> reject unknown keys unless allow_unknown_keys true. Permissive -> coerce and accept where safe, emit warnings. Legacy-shim -> best-effort translation from legacy schemas to TDSL and blurred validation to preserve customer traffic.
3) Error taxonomy: stable error codes (string ids) for each failure class so SDKs & consoles can map to UX: ERR_TDSL_MISSING_REQUIRED, ERR_TDSL_TYPE_MISMATCH, ERR_TDSL_COERCION_FAILED, ERR_TDSL_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION, ERR_TDSL_UNKNOWN_FIELD, ERR_TDSL_SCHEMA_PARSE.
4) Telemetry & observability: each validation error emits telemetry with schema_id, model_id, api_route, client_sdk, validation_mode, and histogram of latency. Avoid logging PII — values redacted by type heuristics.
5) Runtime: integrate TDSL parser into call preprocessing. Provide a lightweight cache keyed by schema hash. Expose API surface to request handlers: validate(params, schema_id, mode) -> {valid:bool, errors:[codes], normalized_params, warnings}.
6) SDKs: implement preflight validation using TDSL subset to fail fast locally with same error codes as server. Fall back to server validation if local validator missing or disabled.
7) Compatibility layer: migration tool that ingests existing JSON Schema / ad-hoc manifests and emits TDSL with best-effort aliases and warnings. CLI: tdsl-migrate --input legacy-manifest.json --output tdsl.yaml --report migration-report.md.
8) Authoring UX: provide schema linter (tdsl-lint), editor snippets (VSCode), and examples for common patterns (tool with nested objects, array unions, optional polymorphism).
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for TDSL parser: valid/invalid constructs, annotation parsing.
- Property-based tests for coercion rules (number<->string, bool variants).
- Integration tests: end-to-end request through SDK -> runtime validation -> tool executor with mocked tool. Verify normalized_params consumed by runtime.
- Regression tests: map 50 representative legacy schemas through migrator and ensure behavior unchanged (using golden traces).
- Chaos tests: enable strict mode in Canary region and assert graceful degradation: requests that previously succeeded under permissive mode are rejected with clear upgrades guidance.
rollout_plan:
1) Internals-only alpha: ship parser and validation in a feature flag, wire telemetry. (Week 1)
2) SDK preflight opt-in: release python/js SDK validators as beta. Invite customers building tools to test. (Week 2-3)
3) Migrate internal Redwood official tools to TDSL and run canary in staging. (Week 3)
4) Legacy shim enablement for existing customers, permissive by default. Publish migration guide and linting tools. (Week 4)
5) Flip default to strict for new schema creation; existing schemas remain legacy-shim for 90 days before upgrade notice. (Week 8)
6) Post-migration: deprecate legacy mode after 120 days from first notice; provide tooling to auto-fix common issues.
risks:
- Overly strict validation might break production traffic if migration isn't coordinated. Mitigation: multi-week permissive period and canarying.
- Telemetry could inadvertently capture sensitive parameter values. Mitigation: redaction heuristics and security review of telemetry fields.
- SDK divergence (behavior mismatch). Mitigation: identical test vectors and shared validation library where possible.
- Performance regression from validation cost under high QPS. Mitigation: LRU schema parser cache, JIT validate only on write-heavy routes, offload expensive checks to background when safe.
notes:
Compatibility examples (excerpt):
TDSL short form example (YAML):
---
name: create_ticket
schema_id: tdsl.create_ticket.v1
params:
  title:
    type: string
    required: true
  description:
    type: string
    required: false
    coerce: true
  priority:
    type: enum
    values: [low, medium, high]
    default: medium
  metadata:
    type: object
    allow_unknown_keys: true
    deprecation_notice: 'metadata.* will be standardized in v2; prefer tags and owner fields.'
---
Behavioral notes: runtime normalizes enums to canonical lowercase tokens; aliases allowed via 'aliases: ["prio", "urgency"]'.
customer_notes: For customers: expect better error messages with actionability (which field failed and why). We will provide a migration CLI and compatibility report. For high-volume producers, coordinate migration windows with our support team.
